title: What is the taxi exam?
summary: The taxi driver exam is an electronic theory exam required for a Finnish taxi driver's permit. It checks whether you understand passenger safety, special passenger needs, customer service situations, and transport and traffic safety.

items.label: Questions
items.value: 50 multiple-choice questions

items.label: Time
items.value: Maximum 45 minutes

items.label: Pass mark
items.value: At least 38 correct answers out of 50, and you must also reach the minimum score in each official topic area.

items.label: Format
items.value: Several answer options per question — only one answer is fully correct.

items.label: Language
items.value: Finnish or Swedish. No interpreter or dictionary may be used in the exam.

items.label: Where
items.value: The exam is arranged by Traficom's service provider. Since 17.11.2025, taxi driver exams are held as group exams in 12 towns: Järvenpää, Oulu, Tampere, Turku, Kuopio, Vaasa, Lappeenranta, Jyväskylä, Lahti, Lohja, Seinäjoki, and Rovaniemi.

items.label: Cost
items.value: The listed taxi driver exam fee is €138.00. Always check the current fee on the booking/payment page before paying.

items.label: Retakes
items.value: If you fail, you can book another exam according to available appointments. If a person commits fraud in the taxi exam, Traficom can impose a 6-month ban from taking the exam.

items.label: Result
items.value: The electronic exam system checks the answers and gives the result decision based on the number of correct answers.

note: The exam is not passed only by reaching 38/50. You must also pass the minimum score in each official topic area.

title: How to get a taxi driver's permit
summary: The taxi driver's permit is called "taksinkuljettajan ajolupa". It is separate from a normal driving licence. You need it before you can legally work as a taxi driver in Finland.

items.label: Step 1
items.value: Hold a category B driving licence that you received at least one year earlier in Finland or another EU/EEA country.

items.label: Step 2
items.value: Make sure you are not under a driving ban.

items.label: Step 3
items.value: Meet the Group 2 medical requirements for drivers.

items.label: Step 4
items.value: Pass the taxi driver exam.

items.label: Step 5
items.value: Pass Traficom's suitability/background check. You must not have criminal or fine-register entries that prevent the permit from being granted.

items.label: Step 6
items.value: Submit the permit application at an Ajovarma service point. Attach the required medical statement and photo if needed.

items.label: Step 7
items.value: Wait for Traficom's decision. The average processing time is about 2 weeks when no extra information is needed. If the permit is granted, the card is normally sent by post.

items.label: Validity
items.value: The taxi driver's permit is normally valid for 5 years. If the driver has reached the age of 68, the permit is valid for 2 years.

items.label: Renewal
items.value: The permit must be renewed before it expires. For renewal, you must still not be under a driving ban, you must meet the Group 2 health requirements, and you must not have disqualifying criminal or fine-register entries.

note: A first-aid course is useful in real taxi work, but it is not listed by Traficom as an official requirement for the taxi driver's permit.

title: The 4 official exam modules
summary: All 50 questions come from four official topic areas. Each area has its own minimum score. If you miss the minimum in even one area, the whole exam fails.

categories.name: Taking care of passenger assistance and safety
categories.description: This section tests the driver's responsibility for the passenger and the transport. It includes safe boarding and exiting, the correct use and securing of safety devices, technical aids, and communication devices during the journey.
keyRules: Passenger assistance, safe entry and exit, safety devices, technical aids, and driver responsibility.

categories.name: Special needs of different passenger groups
categories.description: This section tests how the driver recognises and handles different passengers' assistance needs. It includes disabled passengers, school and daycare transport, elderly passengers, and other passenger groups that may need extra help.
keyRules: Disabled passengers, elderly passengers, children, school/daycare transport, and recognising assistance needs.

categories.name: Customer-service situations in taxi services
categories.description: This section tests professional customer service. It includes passenger comfort, driver behaviour, interaction with the customer, and the driver's general responsibility for the customer during the service situation.
keyRules: Customer interaction, professional behaviour, passenger comfort, and service responsibility.

categories.name: Factors affecting transport and traffic safety
categories.name_fi: Kuljetusten ja liikenteen turvallisuuteen vaikuttavat tekijät
categories.description: This section tests traffic safety and taxi-driving rules. It includes general road safety, taxi-related rules and regulations, and the quality requirements for taxi services.
keyRules: Traffic safety, taxi-driving rules, vehicle/use requirements, and taxi-service quality rules.

note: A score of 38/50 is not enough if one topic area is below its minimum. For example, if your total is 39/50 but you get only 6/10 in Customer Service, the exam fails.

title: On exam day
summary: Know the basic rules before you enter the exam room.

items.label: Bring
items.value: Valid photo ID and any documents required by the booking instructions.

items.label: Arrive
items.value: Arrive early enough to follow the check-in instructions. Late arrival may cause problems with participation.

items.label: Device
items.value: The exam is done electronically. In the current group-exam model, participants complete the exam at the same time on a tablet.

items.label: Allowed
items.value: No phone, headphones, communication devices, recording devices, notes, dictionary, or other materials may be used. The exam cannot be done with an interpreter.

items.label: Language
items.value: You complete the exam in Finnish or Swedish.

items.label: Questions
items.value: Read every word carefully. Finnish exam wording is precise, and small words such as "aina", "vain", "ellei", "jos", and "mikäli" can change the meaning.

items.label: Fraud warning
items.value: Copying, saving, recording, sharing exam questions, using prohibited devices, or trying to get outside help is fraud. Fraud can lead to a 6-month ban from taking the taxi exam.

items.label: Results
items.value: The electronic system checks the answers and gives the result decision immediately.

items.label: App study tip
items.value: If your Finnish is weak, use TaxiPilot's clue-word method. Many questions become easier when you recognise responsibility words, condition words, negative words, and time/order words.
